does: Rolls shaped meatballs lightly in flour and fries them in a shallow layer of oil, turning them, until they are browned on every side. They are then finished in a sauce, where they finish cooking and the flour thickens it a little.
how: Roll each ball in flour and tap off the excess.
Heat a finger's depth of oil in a frying pan until a little flour sizzles at once.
Put the balls in with room between them, and leave them until the underside is brown.
Turn them with spoons or tongs until they are browned all over, then lift them out.
Fry in batches rather than crowd the pan.

cues.text: An even brown crust on every side, with the round shape kept.
A steady sizzle when each ball goes in.

mistakes.mistake: Turning the balls too early, so that the crust tears and they break.
mistakes.fix: Wait until the underside is brown and lets go of the pan.

mistakes.mistake: Crowding the pan, so that the oil cools and the meatballs go pale and greasy.
mistakes.fix: Fry a few at a time.

comes_after.why: The balls must be shaped evenly before they are fried.

variant_of.differs: The food is round and floured, and it is turned on every side to brown, not once, and is not cooked to the centre in the pan.
